message.content:
Implement michi's upgrade from Callisto 0.20.0 to 0.22.0. Repo orin-dx/michi. Branch from `origin/main` as `chore/callisto-0.22`. Read AGENTS.md first (prefix shell commands with `rtk`; comments plain, wrap at 120 cols). Commit when done (conventional message, no session links or Claude-Session trailers), push the branch (normal push; never force, never main). Do NOT open a PR and do NOT trigger any workflow or release. Nothing here may publish anything.

## Sources
- Callisto source: /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto. Use the tag, not HEAD: `git -C /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto show callisto@0.22.0:<path>` (docs/config.md, docs/releasing.md, docs/publishing.md; the `init --workflow` matrix template and code in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs` ~:911-964, `matrix.rs`, `release/mod.rs`, `provider/registry/npm.rs`). Tag commit: callisto@0.22.0 = 9234c02c00f65c7b742da4f4dd8b9fdbfbb0215a. To get the generated reference workflow, prefer building callisto 0.22.0 from a scratch worktree of the callisto repo at that tag (`git -C /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto worktree add $TMPDIR/callisto-0.22 callisto@0.22.0`, `cargo build --release -p <cli crate>`), then run `callisto init --workflow` in a scratch copy of michi (NOT the real worktree) to produce the reference `callisto-release.yml`. If building fails, reconstruct the reference from the template source and say so.

## Prior research findings (verify, don't trust blindly)
1. `callisto.toml` simplifies to roughly: one `[[package]]` for `cargo/michi-core` with `publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]`, `tag-template = "michi@{version}"`, `previous-tag-templates = ["michi-core@{version}"]` (keep the existing explanatory comment), plus the `[[fixed-group]] michi`. `[changesets] dir`, the whole `[cascade]` table (mode/bump-severity/preserve-npm-ranges are defaults; peer-escalation default flipped to false in 0.22 but michi has no peer deps), and every `release-trigger = "changeset"` are defaults. The other three `[[package]]` blocks only set the default `publish-to`; npm's default was not verified — verify in source at the tag; keep any block whose default you cannot confirm. Do not add a `[release]` table (its targets are for cargo binary assets; michi's napi targets come from packages/michi-node/package.json `napi.targets`). Validate the new config with the 0.22 binary if you built it (`callisto status --json` / `callisto config`-style validation / `release plan --dry-run` equivalents) and confirm the package set, publish targets, tags and fixed group are identical to what 0.20 config produced (compare against a 0.21.1 binary if available, or reason from source).
2. Workflow: do NOT regenerate-and-replace. Hand-edit `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` to the 0.22 contract using the generated file as reference: pin all Callisto actions to `@9234c02c00f65c7b742da4f4dd8b9fdbfbb0215a # callisto@0.22.0` with `version: callisto@0.22.0` (currently at :124/127, :151/153, :340/342); builds run with no registry credentials; add the generated jobs michi lacks (credential-free `attest` for napi/binding artifacts, `package-cargo`, `pack-npm` with pnpm set up, which places the binding (`index.js`/`index.d.ts`, gitignored but in package.json `files`) and runs `napi artifacts`, then `callisto release pack-npm`); in `execute` add `release artifact-manifest --seal-npm` and pass `--artifact-manifest`/`--artifact-dir` to `release execute` so npm publishes are sealed (else E306). KEEP michi's customizations the generated workflow lacks: the provenance gate that only a verified merge of `callisto/version-packages` releases (:47-80), `workflow_dispatch` recovery via `release_source_sha` (:12-17), per-SHA concurrency (:23-25), the pnpm `napi build --js index.js --dts index.d.ts` binding build and the zigbuild + hash-pinned ziglang cross-compile (do not switch to `cross` untested), attestation of addon + JS binding and verification with `--signer-workflow`, `CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG`/`NPM_TOKEN`/`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, the receipt handling with `scripts/released-version.sh` (check the 0.22 receipt path/shape; the generated one writes `$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json`), the summary, and the `smoke-published` job. Drop guards the research says 0.22 makes unnecessary only if you confirm it in source (artifact-slot/PyPI guard :174-180, one-napi-dir limit :195-205, the x86_64-apple-darwin runner override :187-193 if 0.22 maps it to a supported runner itself). `PNPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` is obsolete once publishes are `npm publish <tarball>`; use `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` if provenance is wanted. Keep the workflow filename. Every new job: least-privilege `permissions`, pinned action SHAs consistent with how the file already pins third-party actions.
3. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:45` pins `callisto-validate` to 0.20.0: bump to the 0.22.0 SHA/version.
4. Add a one-line status note to `docs/research/callisto-publishing.md` that michi is on 0.22 (it says 0.10/0.12).
5. No changeset (internal CI/config, nothing user-visible).

## Verify
- `actionlint` on the workflow if available (`proto`/`brew` may have it; if not, `npx --yes actionlint` is not valid — use `pipx run`/`go run` only if quick; else say it was not run), and YAML parse (`python3 -c 'import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(...))'`).
- Run the repo's `scripts/test_pending_release_type.py` and `scripts/test_released_version.py` if they touch receipt/decision shapes.
- `just check` (exit code).
- With the built 0.22 binary: validate callisto.toml, and dry-run whatever planning commands work offline to show the plan is unchanged.
- Diff your workflow against the generated reference and list every remaining difference with a one-line reason.

## Report
Branch + commit SHA; the new callisto.toml; a table of workflow jobs (kept / added / changed / removed) with reasons; remaining differences vs the generated reference; what was verified and how; and what can only be verified by a real release (be explicit). Under ~900 words.

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>

[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

mode = "out-of-range"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/michi-core"
# One GitHub release per version for the whole group, attached here and tagged michi@{version}. Callisto keeps a tag
# per package (it finds each package's last release from its own tag and rejects a shared tag, E194), so the other
# members keep {name}@{version}; this mirrors Callisto's own callisto@{version} release tag.
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
release-trigger = "changeset"
tag-template = "michi@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["michi-core@{version}"]

# MIT graph crate, released with the rest of michi (one version for every michi package).
[[package]]
match = "cargo/michi-graph"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# michi-node: NAPI cdylib + npm package
[[package]]
match = "npm/@orin-dx/michi"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Every michi package ships one version: a change to any of them releases all four.
[[fixed-group]]

1	name: Release
  2	
  3	# Callisto's build-matrix release flow for napi platform packages
  4	# (docs/releasing.md in orin-dx/callisto): a push to main either refreshes the
  5	# Callisto version PR or, for a merged version PR, runs plan -> build ->
  6	# execute. Keep this filename: Callisto's recovery docs and coordinator
  7	# identity name `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`.
  8	
  9	on:
 10	  push:
 11	    branches: [main]
 12	  workflow_dispatch:
 13	    inputs:
 14	      release_source_sha:
 15	        description: 'Merged Callisto version-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
 16	        required: false
 17	        type: string
 18	
 19	permissions: {}
 20	
 21	# One group per commit: GitHub replaces a pending run in a shared group, which
 22	# could silently drop a release merge queued behind an unrelated push.
 23	concurrency:
 24	  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
 25	  cancel-in-progress: false
 26	
 27	defaults:
 28	  run:
 29	    shell: bash
 30	
 31	jobs:
 32	  release-candidate:
 33	    name: Identify a merged Callisto version PR
 34	    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
 35	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 36	    permissions:
 37	      contents: read
 38	      pull-requests: read
 39	    outputs:
 40	      is_release: ${{ steps.decision.outputs.is_release }}
 41	      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.release_source_sha }}
 42	      orchestration_sha: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
 43	    steps:
 44	      # Scheduling only: `callisto release plan` verifies the actual
 45	      # parent-to-merge delta. A release must also be a GitHub-verified merge
 46	      # of the managed PR, never a direct push.
 47	      - name: Check release-source provenance
 48	        id: provenance
 49	        env:
 50	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
 51	          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
 52	          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
 53	        run: |
 54	          set -euo pipefail
 55	          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
 56	          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
 57	            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
 58	            exit 1
 59	          fi
 60	          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
 61	          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
 62	            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
 63	            exit 1
 64	          fi
 65	          # gh rejects --slurp together with --jq, so slurp the pages and filter with jq.
 66	          prs=$(gh api --paginate --slurp "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" |
 67	            jq --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" '[.[][] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and
 68	              .head.repo.full_name == $repo and
 69	              (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or
 70	               (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
 71	          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" \
 72	            --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
 73	          managed=false
 74	          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then managed=true; fi
 75	          {
 76	            echo "managed=$managed"
 77	            echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
 78	            # The current run coordinates; a recovery never reruns historic workflow code.
 79	            echo "orchestration_sha=$TRIGGERING_SHA"
 80	          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
 81	
 82	      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
 83	        if: steps.provenance.outputs.managed == 'true'
 84	        with:
 85	          ref: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.release_source_sha }}
 86	          fetch-depth: 2
 87	          persist-credentials: false
 88	
 89	      # `release plan --from-release-commit` requires the commit to write its
 90	      # release decision. A managed PR without one (e.g. a workflow fix merged
 91	      # from a callisto/ branch) refreshes the version PR instead.
 92	      - name: Check for a release decision
 93	        id: decision
 94	        env:
 95	          MANAGED: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.managed }}
 96	        run: |
 97	          set -euo pipefail
 98	          is_release=false
 99	          if [[ "$MANAGED" == true ]] && git rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^ > /dev/null &&
100	            git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only --diff-filter=AM -r HEAD^ HEAD | grep -qxF .callisto/release-decision.json; then
101	            is_release=true
102	          fi
103	          echo "is_release=$is_release" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
104	
105	  version-pr:
106	    name: Create or update the Callisto version PR
107	    needs: release-candidate
108	    if: github.event_name == 'push' && needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release != 'true'
109	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
110	    concurrency:
111	      group: callisto-version-pr
112	      cancel-in-progress: false
113	    permissions:
114	      contents: write
115	      pull-requests: write
116	    steps:
117	      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
118	        with:
119	          fetch-depth: 0
120	          persist-credentials: false
121	
122	      # The default version command (`callisto version`) refreshes lockfiles
123	      # and the action appends --emit-decision .callisto/release-decision.json.
124	      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@aebeedcdaa1dce8f0d9ad1836844ab6be68daf1f # callisto@0.20.0
125	        with:
126	          mode: version-pr
127	          version: callisto@0.20.0
128	          branch: main
129	          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
130	        env:
131	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
132	
133	  plan:
134	    name: Plan the release from the merged version PR
135	    needs: release-candidate
136	    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release == 'true'
137	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
138	    permissions:
139	      contents: read
140	    outputs:
141	      matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
142	      napi_dir: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.napi_dir }}
143	      has_napi: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.has_napi }}
144	    steps:
145	      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
146	        with:
147	          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
148	          fetch-depth: 0
149	          persist-credentials: false
150	
151	      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@aebeedcdaa1dce8f0d9ad1836844ab6be68daf1f # callisto@0.20.0
152	        with:
153	          version: callisto@0.20.0
154	          # Run only a Callisto binary whose attestation verifies; the default falls back to a crates.io build.
155	          verification: require
156	
157	      - name: Plan the release
158	        env:
159	          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
160	          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
161	        run: |
162	          set -euo pipefail
163	          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent"
164	          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json \
165	            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
166	            --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json"
167	          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent" && shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256)
168	
169	      - name: Build the matrix from the intent's napi targets
170	        id: matrix
171	        run: |
172	          set -euo pipefail
173	          intent="$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json"
174	          # This workflow builds napi addons only. Artifact slots or PyPI
175	          # publishes need the generated workflow's artifact-manifest path.
176	          if ! jq -e '(.artifactSlots // []) == [] and
177	            ([.operations[].id.package | select(startswith("pypi/"))] == [])' "$intent" > /dev/null; then
178	            echo "::error::the release intent declares artifact slots or PyPI publishes, which this workflow does not build"
179	            exit 1
180	          fi
181	          # Only packages in the release intent: an unrelated addon adds no build.
182	          {
183	            while IFS= read -r package; do
184	              callisto --format json matrix --package "$package"
185	            done < <(jq -r '[.operations[].id.package] | unique[]' "$intent")
186	          } | jq -s '{platformTargets: (map(.platformTargets) | add // {})}' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/matrix.json"
187	          # Callisto 0.11 schedules x86_64-apple-darwin on macos-13, a retired
188	          # runner image: build it on the arm64 macos-latest instead, where
189	          # rustup's x86_64-apple-darwin target links with Apple's universal SDK.
190	          # Every other target keeps Callisto's hostRunner/useCross (aarch64
191	          # Linux cross-compiles with cargo-zigbuild on ubuntu-latest).
192	          matrix=$(jq -c '[.platformTargets[] | select(.kind == "napi") | .targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName) |
193	            map(if .triple == "x86_64-apple-darwin" then .hostRunner = "macos-latest" | .useCross = false else . end)' \
194	            "$RUNNER_TEMP/matrix.json")
195	          # Execute places one package's JS binding; a second addon needs per-package placement. A release with no
196	          # addon skips the build and placement entirely (the fixed group always includes the npm package today).
197	          napi_dirs=$(jq -c '[.[].packageDir] | unique' <<< "$matrix")
198	          case $(jq length <<< "$napi_dirs") in
199	            0) has_napi=false napi_dir="" ;;
200	            1) has_napi=true napi_dir=$(jq -r '.[0]' <<< "$napi_dirs") ;;
201	            *)
202	              echo "::error::expected at most one napi package directory, got $napi_dirs"
203	              exit 1
204	              ;;
205	          esac
206	          {
207	            echo "matrix=$matrix"
208	            echo "napi_dir=$napi_dir"
209	            echo "has_napi=$has_napi"
210	          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
211	
212	      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
213	        with:
214	          name: release-intent
215	          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
216	          if-no-files-found: error
217	          retention-days: 7
218	
219	  build:
220	    name: Build ${{ matrix.triple }}
221	    needs: [release-candidate, plan]
222	    # An empty matrix is an error in GitHub Actions, so a release without an addon skips the job instead.
223	    if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
224	    strategy:
225	      fail-fast: false
226	      matrix:
227	        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix) }}
228	    runs-on: ${{ matrix.hostRunner }}
229	    permissions:
230	      contents: read
231	      attestations: write
232	      id-token: write
233	    env:
234	      TRIPLE: ${{ matrix.triple }}
235	      USE_CROSS: ${{ matrix.useCross }}
236	    defaults:
237	      run:
238	        working-directory: ${{ matrix.packageDir }}
239	    steps:
240	      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
241	        with:
242	          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
243	          persist-credentials: false
244	
245	      - name: Install the Rust target
246	        run: rustup target add "$TRIPLE"
247	
248	      # Known gap: this composite runs moonrepo/setup-toolchain@v0 (floating tag, pinned only by the composite's own
249	      # SHA), which downloads and runs the proto and moon install scripts from moonrepo/moon's master branch
250	      # ("Installing `moon` globally", because .moon/ exists). Neither can be pinned from here: the script URL is
251	      # hardcoded in that action, and the only inputs (proto-version, moon-version) pick the release the script
252	      # fetches, not the script itself. Replacing the composite with a pinned setup-toolchain would still run the
253	      # proto script, and auto-install would add rust to the proto installs. These jobs never call moon.
254	      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
255	        with:
256	          working-directory: ${{ matrix.packageDir }}
257	          cache: 'false'
258	
259	      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
260	
261	      # napi's --cross-compile links non-native Linux targets with cargo-zigbuild. This job holds id-token and
262	      # attestations: write, so the linker is pinned by version and wheel hash (x86_64 and aarch64 Linux runners).
263	      # Bump both together from the ziglang release page on PyPI.
264	      - name: Install zig
265	        if: matrix.useCross
266	        run: |
267	          set -euo pipefail
268	          pip install --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: -r /dev/stdin <<'REQS'
269	          ziglang==0.17.1 \
270	            --hash=sha256:ea6cc5d87b033cf0aedfbc8f9549a908cae6c50ac31f1698188fa48a74524b54 \
271	            --hash=sha256:b7c5f02fccd40f89b999ee16a1f5ddced56e6182370f8affe494bcf8a28cf07e
272	          REQS
273	
274	      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cfdb7ed4ccc7c7dce37759eae89dc5674b469b39 # v2
275	        if: matrix.useCross
276	        with:
277	          tool: cargo-zigbuild
278	
279	      # --output-dir keeps the checkout clean; napi writes the .node file and
280	      # the generated index.js/index.d.ts there.
281	      - name: Build the napi addon
282	        run: |
283	          set -euo pipefail
284	          args=(--release --target "$TRIPLE" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/napi-out")
285	          if [[ "$USE_CROSS" == true ]]; then args+=(--cross-compile); fi
286	          pnpm build "${args[@]}"
287	
288	      # Sign the bytes that get published (the addon and the JS loader that requires it); the execute job verifies
289	      # them before it holds any registry credential.
290	      - name: Attest the napi addon and JS binding
291	        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
292	        with:
293	          subject-path: |
294	            ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/*.node
295	            ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/index.js
296	            ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/index.d.ts
297	
298	      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
299	        with:
300	          name: napi-${{ matrix.artifactName }}
301	          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/*.node
302	          if-no-files-found: error
303	          retention-days: 7
304	
305	      # index.js and index.d.ts are gitignored build outputs the npm package ships.
306	      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
307	        with:
308	          name: binding-${{ matrix.artifactName }}
309	          path: |
310	            ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/index.js
311	            ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/index.d.ts
312	          if-no-files-found: error
313	          retention-days: 7
314	
315	  execute:
316	    name: Execute the planned release
317	    needs: [release-candidate, plan, build]
318	    # !cancelled() rather than always(): cancelling the run must stop the one irreversible job.
319	    if: >-
320	      !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' &&
321	      (needs.build.result == 'success' || (needs.build.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'false'))
322	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
323	    concurrency:
324	      group: callisto-release-execute
325	      cancel-in-progress: false
326	    permissions:
327	      attestations: read
328	      contents: write
329	      id-token: write
330	    outputs:
331	      smoke_version: ${{ steps.published.outputs.version }}
332	    steps:
333	      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
334	        with:
335	          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
336	          fetch-depth: 0
337	          # Callisto pushes the release tags from this checkout.
338	          persist-credentials: true # zizmor: ignore[artipacked]
339	
340	      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@aebeedcdaa1dce8f0d9ad1836844ab6be68daf1f # callisto@0.20.0
341	        with:
342	          version: callisto@0.20.0
343	          verification: require
344	
345	      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
346	        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
347	        with:
348	          working-directory: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.napi_dir }}
349	          cache: 'false'
350	
351	      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
352	        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
353	        working-directory: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.napi_dir }}
354	
355	      # Downloads land under $RUNNER_TEMP: `release execute` requires a clean worktree.
356	      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
357	        with:
358	          name: release-intent
359	          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
360	
361	      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
362	        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
363	        with:
364	          pattern: napi-*
365	          merge-multiple: true
366	          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-artifacts
367	
368	      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
369	        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
370	        with:
371	          pattern: binding-*
372	          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-bindings
373	
374	      - name: Verify the handoff
375	        run: (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
376	
377	      # Verification pins the signing workflow and this commit's SHA, not the run ID. A binary built by another
378	      # workflow, or by this workflow at a different commit, fails here, before placement; a build from another run
379	      # of this workflow at the same commit would pass.
380	      - name: Verify the napi addon attestations
381	        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
382	        env:
383	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
384	        run: |
385	          set -euo pipefail
386	          shopt -s nullglob
387	          addons=("$RUNNER_TEMP"/napi-artifacts/*.node)
388	          if [[ "${#addons[@]}" -eq 0 ]]; then
389	            echo "::error::no napi addons to verify"
390	            exit 1
391	          fi
392	          for addon in "${addons[@]}"; do
393	            gh attestation verify "$addon" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
394	              --signer-workflow "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml" \
395	              --signer-digest "$GITHUB_SHA" --source-digest "$GITHUB_SHA" --deny-self-hosted-runners
396	          done
397	
398	      # Same check for the JS loader every consumer runs first. Each matrix leg attested its own copy, so verify all.
399	      - name: Verify the JS binding attestations
400	        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
401	        env:
402	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
403	        run: |
404	          set -euo pipefail
405	          shopt -s nullglob
406	          files=("$RUNNER_TEMP"/napi-bindings/*/index.js "$RUNNER_TEMP"/napi-bindings/*/index.d.ts)
407	          if [[ "${#files[@]}" -eq 0 ]]; then
408	            echo "::error::no JS bindings to verify"
409	            exit 1
410	          fi
411	          for file in "${files[@]}"; do
412	            gh attestation verify "$file" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
413	              --signer-workflow "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml" \
414	              --signer-digest "$GITHUB_SHA" --source-digest "$GITHUB_SHA" --deny-self-hosted-runners
415	          done
416	
417	      # Everything placed here is gitignored, so the checkout stays clean:
418	      # the .node files go into the committed npm/<platform> package dirs.
419	      - name: Place the napi artifacts
420	        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
421	        working-directory: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.napi_dir }}
422	        run: |
423	          set -euo pipefail
424	          bindings=("$RUNNER_TEMP"/napi-bindings/*)
425	          for binding in "${bindings[@]}"; do
426	            cmp "${bindings[0]}/index.js" "$binding/index.js"
427	            cmp "${bindings[0]}/index.d.ts" "$binding/index.d.ts"
428	          done
429	          cp "${bindings[0]}/index.js" "${bindings[0]}/index.d.ts" .
430	          # napi 3.7 joins --output-dir onto the package directory, so pass it relative.
431	          pnpm exec napi artifacts --output-dir "$(realpath --relative-to="$PWD" "$RUNNER_TEMP/napi-artifacts")"
432	          for manifest in npm/*/package.json; do
433	            binary="$(dirname "$manifest")/$(jq -r .main "$manifest")"
434	            if [[ ! -f "$binary" ]]; then
435	              echo "::error::missing napi artifact $binary"
436	              exit 1
437	            fi
438	          done
439	          if [[ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]]; then
440	            git status --porcelain
441	            echo "::error::artifact placement dirtied the release checkout"
442	            exit 1
443	          fi
444	
445	      # CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN and NPM_TOKEN are long-lived secrets because Callisto has no OIDC trusted publishing yet,
446	      # so they cannot be dropped here. Revisit when it does (the job already holds id-token: write).
447	      - name: Execute the release
448	        env:
449	          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
450	          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
451	          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: 'true'
452	          # pnpm 11 publishes the main package natively and ignores NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE (npm, which publishes the six
453	          # platform packages, honours it). Without this, @orin-dx/michi shipped with no attestation through 0.7.1.
454	          PNPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: 'true'
455	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
456	          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
457	        run: |

443	          fi
444	
445	      # CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN and NPM_TOKEN are long-lived secrets because Callisto has no OIDC trusted publishing yet,

447	      - name: Execute the release
448	        env:
449	          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
450	          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
451	          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: 'true'

470	      # Callisto writes the receipt only after every selected operation succeeded. A registry publish that landed in

# Releasing

How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.

For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).

---

## Local release: `callisto release`

`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.

- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
- `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, all distributions of each (naming `npm/dual` also releases `cargo/dual`), plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
- It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
- It requires the git repository root to be the workspace root; a workspace in a subdirectory fails with `E170`.
- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
- A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.

`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.

A local release refuses with E320, before any effect, when the registry already holds a version it would release but the package's files changed since the commit that set that version, or no commit in this history sets it. Check out the version commit the error names and run `callisto release` again: it adopts the published version and tags that commit. When no commit is named, check out the commit that was published, or tag it by hand.

### Current retry limit

If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` at the same commit lists the package again, observes each remaining effect and finishes it.

- `Nothing to release.` is not proof of completion for a tag on an older commit: the retry looks only at tags on the commit being released.
- CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.

---

## Generated workflows

`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`; in a workspace that already has `callisto.toml` it writes only the workflow. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.

Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.

- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `package` (no secrets) checks whether the commit adds or modifies the release decision, and if so plans the release, builds Python distributions and packs npm packages, and hands them to `execute`, which publishes exactly those files. On that push `version-pr` waits for `execute`, so the next release PR is built from the new tags. A push that merely contains an untagged version publishes nothing; recovery is "Re-run failed jobs".
- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan, build (read-only), attest (no checkout, no commands), optional Python build, crate packaging and npm pack jobs (no credentials), and execute. As in the simple shape, `version-pr` waits for `execute` on a release push. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.

Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).

Generated build support has these boundaries:

- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
- Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.

The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.

Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. The action installs the release that commit belongs to. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.

Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
- npm lifecycle hooks split at the pack. `prepack` and `prepare` run in the job that packs the package, which holds no registry credentials. The publish is `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`, so `prepublishOnly`, `publish` and `postpublish` no longer run. Move work that must happen before a release into `prepack`, and anything that acts on the registry into a step of your own after `execute`. Effects an owner-defined hook still has at pack time are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

During a pre cycle (`callisto pre enter <tag>`) the release PR works the same way: a new changeset, or a new conventional commit to a `release-trigger = "auto"` package, opens or updates the release PR for the next prerelease, a cycle with nothing new since its last prerelease needs none, and after `callisto pre exit` the release PR releases the stable versions.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for a hand-written local workflow, and `execute` runs `callisto release execute` on the intent and files a credential-free job prepared. Generated workflows use plan/build/execute (build-matrix) or package/execute (simple). See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials or an OIDC token for publishing. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning, build, pack and attestation jobs, and action inputs. The attestation job holds `id-token: write`, so it has no checkout and runs no command.

After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

## PR pre-flight verification

[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:

- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
- `callisto status --check --since origin/main` — also fails when the pull request changes a package that no changeset names. A change that needs no release takes a changeset with severity `none`.
- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.

---

## Release identity and recovery

Every release run records two different revisions:

- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.

A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and the merged release PR's full source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code or invent a newer version. Callisto's own workflow asks [`callisto release pending`](#finding-releases-that-did-not-finish) for the oldest unfinished release on each main push. It verifies that SHA against the merged managed PR and the current main history before planning. After a release executes, the workflow dispatches the next unfinished one, or refreshes the release PR for newer changesets when none remains.

To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs" or dispatch the workflow on main with `release_source_sha=<merged PR merge SHA>`. Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds. The merge SHA is available in the PR's merge commit and does not depend on a proposed version tag. Release runs execute one at a time: a push during a release waits, then finds nothing pending. A dispatch with an explicit SHA queued behind a push can be replaced by it, so dispatch it again if it did not start.

A failed release is selected again on every main push until it finishes, which also holds back the release PR refresh. To get past one you finished by hand, push its missing tags, or run `callisto release pending --from <newer release sha>`. Otherwise recover it with a dispatch of its SHA (see [recovering an older release](#recovering-an-older-release)). Finish an older unpublished release before merging a newer release PR: the newer one publishes without any warning that the older version was never tagged.

Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.

## Finding releases that did not finish

`callisto release pending` lists the merged release commits whose release did not finish, oldest first, with what is missing. It reads each release commit's committed decision and checks that every package has its tag and every GitHub release is published, so it needs no checkout of the old commit and publishes nothing. A release publishes to the registries before it tags, so a missing tag means the release stopped early.

```sh
callisto release pending                    # text
callisto --format json release pending      # for a workflow
callisto release pending --from <sha>       # skip an older release that cannot finish
```

Recover each one with the dispatch below, oldest first.

## A stale release PR

Callisto's workflow rebuilds the release PR on every push to `main`. While that rebuild is pending the PR is stale: if changesets changed on `main` since it was built, merging it releases the wrong set. So a second workflow, `Hold release PR`, turns the open release PR into a draft the moment `main` moves, and the release workflow marks it ready only after a rebuild from the new tip. If the rebuild fails, the PR stays a draft and cannot be merged. Re-run that `Release` workflow run, and the PR becomes ready when it succeeds. A transient GitHub error during the rebuild is attempted up to four times in all before it fails.

If a stale release PR whose changesets were already consumed on `main` was merged anyway, the release fails with [E165](errors.md) because the changesets the merge deleted are not the ones its decision recorded, and every later push to `main` retries it. A stale PR that deletes no changesets, one that releases only bumps inferred from commits or a prerelease PR of a Changesets v2 pre cycle, gets no E165 from its changesets. E165 still refuses it when `main` already holds its versions, and `Hold release PR` keeps a stale PR in draft. Nothing was published. Revert the merge's release payload (the version bumps, changelog entries and `.callisto/release-decision.json`, not the changeset files) in a pull request to `main`. The next push rebuilds the release PR from the changesets that are really pending.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh
gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

## Publication checks

Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.

Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.

---

## Platform-package publish order

`callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.

A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.

- **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
- **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.

For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.
# Publishing: registry authentication

Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).

Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.

---

## First publish

A package that has never been published is released from its manifest version with no changeset. Callisto plans it like any other release, and the first publish is the one most likely to fail for reasons outside Callisto:

- **Check the name first.** A name another project already owns is rejected by the registry. If it already holds the version you are releasing under another repository, `callisto release` stops with E322 and names that repository. Search the registry before the first release.
- **Fill in the metadata the registry requires.** crates.io needs `description` and `license` (or `license-file`) in `Cargo.toml`. A first release of a crate without them stops with E323 before anything is published.
- **Use a token that can create the package.** A token scoped to existing packages cannot publish a new one. Trusted publishing (OIDC) is configured per package on the registry and generally needs the package, or a pending publisher, to exist first, so plan on one token-based first publish. Follow each registry's current documentation.
- **Package managers.** An npm package is packed with the manager its workspace uses (`npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` 4 or `bun`), so `workspace:` and `catalog:` ranges are rewritten in the tarball, and published by `npm` as `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`, passing `--tag`, `--access` and `--registry` when set. Authentication is `npm`'s: `NPM_TOKEN` through the project or user `.npmrc`, so a token kept only in `.yarnrc.yml` (`npmAuthToken`) or Bun's config is not used. `npm publish <tarball>` does not read a registry from `.yarnrc.yml` (`npmPublishRegistry`, `npmRegistryServer`, or either under `npmScopes`) or from `bunfig.toml`, so a yarn or bun workspace that sets one there is refused with E168 before anything is published. Set the registry as `publishConfig.registry` in the package's `package.json`, or in `.npmrc`.
- **Scoped npm packages** publish with `--access public` by default. A private scoped package sets `publishConfig.access` to `"restricted"` in its `package.json`, which Callisto passes through.
- **Rehearse.** `callisto release --dry-run` shows what would be published and in which order, and works without credentials.

## Pulling a release

Callisto never deletes, yanks or deprecates anything. Pulling a release is a manual registry action, and the version stays used:

| Registry | Soft pull | Delete |
| --- | --- | --- |
| crates.io | `cargo yank` hides it from new resolution; it stays downloadable and existing lockfiles keep working. | Limited to 72 hours after publishing, or a single owner, few downloads and no dependents. |
| npm | `npm deprecate` keeps it installable with a warning. | `npm unpublish` within 72 hours if nothing depends on it; later only with no dependents, under 300 weekly downloads and a single owner. A used version number can never be reused, and removing every version blocks the name for 24 hours. |
| PyPI | Yank (PEP 592) hides it from normal resolution. | Permanent. A filename cannot be reused even after deletion, and deleting a project frees its name for anyone. |

Registries cache their indexes for minutes, so a pulled version can keep appearing briefly. Prefer the soft pull, then release a fixed, higher version through the normal flow. Leave the git tag in place: Callisto treats an existing tag as a release already made. Yanking does not undo a leaked secret; rotate it.

If you remove a version that is still the manifest version, `callisto release` will try to finish it again and stop with an error. Bump the version with a changeset instead.

See the registries' own pages for current rules: [cargo yank](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-yank.html), [npm unpublish](https://docs.npmjs.com/policies/unpublish) and the [PyPI help](https://pypi.org/help/).

## Where a publish goes

A registry with no `url` in `callisto.toml` publishes wherever the checkout's own configuration says: `.npmrc` for npm. Callisto honors that on purpose, so a private registry set there keeps working, and it means that file decides where the registry token is sent. A Cargo package with `crates-io` in `publish-to` runs a plain `cargo publish`, so Cargo's own configuration (`publish` in `Cargo.toml`, `[registry] default`) can redirect it while Callisto still observes crates.io. To pin a destination, name a `[registries.<name>]` entry with `kind = "cargo"` in `publish-to`: Callisto then runs `cargo publish --registry <name>`, `.cargo/config.toml` decides that registry's URL and where its token is sent, and the release job needs `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN` (the name upper-cased, `-` as `_`). Review changes to them like code. A release pull request cannot carry such a change: a version commit may only touch manifests, lockfiles, changelogs, changesets and the decision file, and any other path fails verification with E165. For npm (except yarn) and PyPI, `url` on the registry entry names the registry Callisto reads and publishes to from `callisto.toml`. It does not override native routing: npm configuration such as `@scope:registry` in `.npmrc` still routes a scoped package, and Callisto respects that. Callisto adds no destination allowlist or preflight, so review changes to `.npmrc` like code. A named Cargo registry takes its URL only from `.cargo/config.toml`, and a `url` on a cargo registry is rejected.

---

## npm

Two supported patterns.

### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`

Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate with npm registry
  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
  env:
    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
```

`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.

### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`

`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: '20'
    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.

### Choosing a pattern

| Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
| Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
| Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
| Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |

### Provenance

Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.

### Tokenless trusted publishing

npm and PyPI can publish without a stored token: the registry trusts the workflow's OIDC identity. The native tools own that authentication. Callisto adds no auth switch or broker; it keeps the `execute` job's OIDC request variables for `npm` and `twine`, and when `NPM_TOKEN` or `PYPI_TOKEN` is empty or unset it configures no token, so the tool falls back to OIDC.

Hosted OIDC publishing is not yet verified against the real registries. Rehearse it on a throwaway package before relying on it.

1. **Registry side.** Add a trusted publisher for the package on the registry.
   - npm: bind it to the release workflow file (`callisto-release.yml`), and to the GitHub environment too if the `execute` job uses one.
   - PyPI: add a trusted publisher naming the repository, the workflow file and, if used, the environment. A package that does not exist yet needs a pending publisher.
2. **Workflow side.**
   - `execute` needs `permissions: id-token: write`; generated workflows grant it.
   - Do not set the `NPM_TOKEN` or `PYPI_TOKEN` secret. Remove it, or leave the repository secret undefined.
   - npm needs Node 22.14 or newer and npm 11.5.1 or newer for trusted publishing. Add a setup step to the `execute` job before the release step, for example:

     ```yaml
     - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 # pin to a commit SHA
       with:
         node-version: '22.14'
     - run: npm install --global npm@^11.5.1
     ```

   - PyPI needs a twine that supports trusted publishing. Generated workflows install `twine==7.0.0` in `execute`; a hand-written workflow must provide its own. Older twine releases were not checked.
3. **Limit.** With no token Callisto passes no `.npmrc` to the confirmation step, so a restricted scoped package may publish and then fail to confirm, because npm answers an anonymous view of it with 404. Not yet verified.
4. **Read auth stays separate.** Trusted publishing covers publishing only. A job that installs private dependencies still needs its own read credential (for example an `.npmrc` token with read access or a private index login) in the job that installs them, never in `execute`.

---

## Cargo (crates.io)

Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:

```yaml
env:
  CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
```

Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. Inject it only into the job that publishes.

---

## Python (PyPI)

Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):

```yaml
env:
  TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
  TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
```

Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognize that variable name.

The release action maps the `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_USERNAME` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` itself. A workflow that runs `twine` directly must set both, because the secret name alone does not configure Twine.

### Generated Callisto workflows

Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing: `NPM_TOKEN` becomes an `.npmrc` entry that reads it, and `PYPI_TOKEN` becomes `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` with `TWINE_PASSWORD`. An unset or empty secret configures nothing, which leaves [tokenless trusted publishing](#tokenless-trusted-publishing) to the tools. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.

`prepack` and `prepare` run in the job that packs the package, which has no registry credentials. `prepublishOnly`, `publish` and `postpublish` do not run, because the publish is `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`. A package that relied on a publish-time hook moves that work into `prepack`.

Without a manifest (the local `callisto release`), the files are built in a temporary directory with registry credentials withheld, then uploaded. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).
- npm is sealed the same way: `release pack-npm` packs each npm package and platform package, `artifact-manifest --seal-npm` records the tarballs, and `execute` publishes exactly those files after re-checking their sha256. A rerun in the same workflow run reuses the same tarballs; "Re-run all jobs" packs again, and a version the registry already shows is adopted by version, not by bytes.

34	## Generated workflows
35	
36	`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`; in a workspace that already has `callisto.toml` it writes only the workflow. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.
37	
38	Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.
39	
40	- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. 41	- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan, build (read-only), attest (no checkout, no commands), optional Python build, crate packaging and npm pack jobs (no credentials), and execute. 42	- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.
43	
44	Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).

47	
48	- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
49	- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.

51	- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.
52	
53	The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.
54	
55	Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.

60	- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
61	- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.

67	## Release PR and approval
68	
69	The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.
70	
71	During a pre cycle (`callisto pre enter <tag>`) the release PR works the same way: a new changeset, or a new conventional commit to a `release-trigger = "auto"` package, opens or updates the release PR for the next prerelease, a cycle with nothing new since its last prerelease needs none, and after `callisto pre exit` the release PR releases the stable versions.
72	
73	The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for a hand-written local workflow, and `execute` runs `callisto release execute` on the intent and files a credential-free job prepared. Generated workflows use plan/build/execute (build-matrix) or package/execute (simple). See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).
74	
75	Only `execute` receives registry credentials or an OIDC token for publishing. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning, build, pack and attestation jobs, and action inputs. The attestation job holds `id-token: write`, so it has no checkout and runs no command.
76	
77	After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

79	## PR pre-flight verification
80	
81	[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:
82	
83	- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
84	- `callisto status --check --since origin/main` — also fails when the pull request changes a package that no changeset names. A change that needs no release takes a changeset with severity `none`.
85	- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
86	- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.
