89	
90	## Release identity and recovery
91	
92	Every release run records two different revisions:
93	
94	- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
95	- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.
96	
97	A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and the merged release PR's full source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code or invent a newer version. Callisto's own workflow asks [`callisto release pending`](#finding-releases-that-did-not-finish) for the oldest unfinished release on each main push. It verifies that SHA against the merged managed PR and the current main history before planning. After a release executes, the workflow dispatches the next unfinished one, or refreshes the release PR for newer changesets when none remains.
98	
99	To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs" or dispatch the workflow on main with `release_source_sha=<merged PR merge SHA>`. Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds. The merge SHA is available in the PR's merge commit and does not depend on a proposed version tag. Release runs execute one at a time: a push during a release waits, then finds nothing pending. A dispatch with an explicit SHA queued behind a push can be replaced by it, so dispatch it again if it did not start.
100	
101	A failed release is selected again on every main push until it finishes, which also holds back the release PR refresh. To get past one you finished by hand, push its missing tags, or run `callisto release pending --from <newer release sha>`. Otherwise recover it with a dispatch of its SHA (see [recovering an older release](#recovering-an-older-release)). Finish an older unpublished release before merging a newer release PR: the newer one publishes without any warning that the older version was never tagged.
102	
103	Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.
104	
105	## Finding releases that did not finish
106	
107	`callisto release pending` lists the merged release commits whose release did not finish, oldest first, with what is missing. It reads each release commit's committed decision and checks that every package has its tag and every GitHub release is published, so it needs no checkout of the old commit and publishes nothing. A release publishes to the registries before it tags, so a missing tag means the release stopped early.
108	
109	```sh
110	callisto release pending                    # text
111	callisto --format json release pending      # for a workflow
112	callisto release pending --from <sha>       # skip an older release that cannot finish
113	```
114	
115	Recover each one with the dispatch below, oldest first.
116	
117	## A stale release PR
118	
119	Callisto's workflow rebuilds the release PR on every push to `main`. While that rebuild is pending the PR is stale: if changesets changed on `main` since it was built, merging it releases the wrong set. So a second workflow, `Hold release PR`, turns the open release PR into a draft the moment `main` moves, and the release workflow marks it ready only after a rebuild from the new tip. If the rebuild fails, the PR stays a draft and cannot be merged. Re-run that `Release` workflow run, and the PR becomes ready when it succeeds. A transient GitHub error during the rebuild is attempted up to four times in all before it fails.
120	
121	If a stale release PR whose changesets were already consumed on `main` was merged anyway, the release fails with [E165](errors.md) because the changesets the merge deleted are not the ones its decision recorded, and every later push to `main` retries it. A stale PR that deletes no changesets, one that releases only bumps inferred from commits or a prerelease PR of a Changesets v2 pre cycle, gets no E165 from its changesets. E165 still refuses it when `main` already holds its versions, and `Hold release PR` keeps a stale PR in draft. Nothing was published. Revert the merge's release payload (the version bumps, changelog entries and `.callisto/release-decision.json`, not the changeset files) in a pull request to `main`. The next push rebuilds the release PR from the changesets that are really pending.
122	
123	## Recovering an older release
124	
125	Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:
126	
127	**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:
128	
129	```sh
130	SHA=<release-source sha>
131	git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
132	git push origin "<tag>"
133	gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
134	```
135	
136	**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:
137	
138	```sh
139	gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
140	gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
141	```
142	
143	## Publication checks
144	
145	Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.
146	
147	Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).
148	
149	GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.
150	
151	---
152	
153	## Platform-package publish order
154	
155	`callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.
156	
157	A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.
158	
159	- **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
160	- **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.
161	
162	For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.
163	# Publishing: registry authentication
164	
165	Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).
166	
167	Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## First publish
172	
173	A package that has never been published is released from its manifest version with no changeset. Callisto plans it like any other release, and the first publish is the one most likely to fail for reasons outside Callisto:
174	
175	- **Check the name first.** A name another project already owns is rejected by the registry. If it already holds the version you are releasing under another repository, `callisto release` stops with E322 and names that repository. Search the registry before the first release.
176	- **Fill in the metadata the registry requires.** crates.io needs `description` and `license` (or `license-file`) in `Cargo.toml`. A first release of a crate without them stops with E323 before anything is published.
177	- **Use a token that can create the package.** A token scoped to existing packages cannot publish a new one. Trusted publishing (OIDC) is configured per package on the registry and generally needs the package, or a pending publisher, to exist first, so plan on one token-based first publish. Follow each registry's current documentation.
178	- **Package managers.** An npm package is packed with the manager its workspace uses (`npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` 4 or `bun`), so `workspace:` and `catalog:` ranges are rewritten in the tarball, and published by `npm` as `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`, passing `--tag`, `--access` and `--registry` when set. Authentication is `npm`'s: `NPM_TOKEN` through the project or user `.npmrc`, so a token kept only in `.yarnrc.yml` (`npmAuthToken`) or Bun's config is not used. `npm publish <tarball>` does not read a registry from `.yarnrc.yml` (`npmPublishRegistry`, `npmRegistryServer`, or either under `npmScopes`) or from `bunfig.toml`, so a yarn or bun workspace that sets one there is refused with E168 before anything is published. Set the registry as `publishConfig.registry` in the package's `package.json`, or in `.npmrc`.
179	- **Scoped npm packages** publish with `--access public` by default. A private scoped package sets `publishConfig.access` to `"restricted"` in its `package.json`, which Callisto passes through.
180	- **Rehearse.** `callisto release --dry-run` shows what would be published and in which order, and works without credentials.
181	
182	## Pulling a release
183	
184	Callisto never deletes, yanks or deprecates anything. Pulling a release is a manual registry action, and the version stays used:
185	
186	| Registry | Soft pull | Delete |
187	| --- | --- | --- |
188	| crates.io | `cargo yank` hides it from new resolution; it stays downloadable and existing lockfiles keep working. | Limited to 72 hours after publishing, or a single owner, few downloads and no dependents. |
189	| npm | `npm deprecate` keeps it installable with a warning. | `npm unpublish` within 72 hours if nothing depends on it; later only with no dependents, under 300 weekly downloads and a single owner. A used version number can never be reused, and removing every version blocks the name for 24 hours. |
190	| PyPI | Yank (PEP 592) hides it from normal resolution. | Permanent. A filename cannot be reused even after deletion, and deleting a project frees its name for anyone. |
191	
192	Registries cache their indexes for minutes, so a pulled version can keep appearing briefly. Prefer the soft pull, then release a fixed, higher version through the normal flow. Leave the git tag in place: Callisto treats an existing tag as a release already made. Yanking does not undo a leaked secret; rotate it.
193	
194	If you remove a version that is still the manifest version, `callisto release` will try to finish it again and stop with an error. Bump the version with a changeset instead.
195	
196	See the registries' own pages for current rules: [cargo yank](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-yank.html), [npm unpublish](https://docs.npmjs.com/policies/unpublish) and the [PyPI help](https://pypi.org/help/).
197	
198	## Where a publish goes
199	
200	A registry with no `url` in `callisto.toml` publishes wherever the checkout's own configuration says: `.npmrc` for npm. Callisto honors that on purpose, so a private registry set there keeps working, and it means that file decides where the registry token is sent. A Cargo package with `crates-io` in `publish-to` runs a plain `cargo publish`, so Cargo's own configuration (`publish` in `Cargo.toml`, `[registry] default`) can redirect it while Callisto still observes crates.io. To pin a destination, name a `[registries.<name>]` entry with `kind = "cargo"` in `publish-to`: Callisto then runs `cargo publish --registry <name>`, `.cargo/config.toml` decides that registry's URL and where its token is sent, and the release job needs `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN` (the name upper-cased, `-` as `_`). Review changes to them like code. A release pull request cannot carry such a change: a version commit may only touch manifests, lockfiles, changelogs, changesets and the decision file, and any other path fails verification with E165. For npm (except yarn) and PyPI, `url` on the registry entry names the registry Callisto reads and publishes to from `callisto.toml`. It does not override native routing: npm configuration such as `@scope:registry` in `.npmrc` still routes a scoped package, and Callisto respects that. Callisto adds no destination allowlist or preflight, so review changes to `.npmrc` like code. A named Cargo registry takes its URL only from `.cargo/config.toml`, and a `url` on a cargo registry is rejected.
201	
202	---
203	
204	## npm
205	
206	Two supported patterns.
207	
208	### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`
209	
210	Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:
211	
212	```yaml
213	- name: Authenticate with npm registry
214	  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
215	  env:
216	    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
217	
218	- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
219	```
220	
221	`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.
222	
223	### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`
224	
225	`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:
226	
227	```yaml
228	- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
229	  with:
230	    node-version: '20'
231	    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
232	
233	- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
234	  env:
235	    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
236	```
237	
238	`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.
239	
240	### Choosing a pattern
241	
242	| Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
243	| --- | --- | --- |
244	| Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
245	| Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
246	| Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
247	| Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |
248	
249	### Provenance
250	
251	Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.
252	
253	### Tokenless trusted publishing
254	
255	npm and PyPI can publish without a stored token: the registry trusts the workflow's OIDC identity. The native tools own that authentication. Callisto adds no auth switch or broker; it keeps the `execute` job's OIDC request variables for `npm` and `twine`, and when `NPM_TOKEN` or `PYPI_TOKEN` is empty or unset it configures no token, so the tool falls back to OIDC.
256	
257	Hosted OIDC publishing is not yet verified against the real registries. Rehearse it on a throwaway package before relying on it.
258	
259	1. **Registry side.** Add a trusted publisher for the package on the registry.
260	   - npm: bind it to the release workflow file (`callisto-release.yml`), and to the GitHub environment too if the `execute` job uses one.
261	   - PyPI: add a trusted publisher naming the repository, the workflow file and, if used, the environment. A package that does not exist yet needs a pending publisher.
262	2. **Workflow side.**
263	   - `execute` needs `permissions: id-token: write`; generated workflows grant it.
264	   - Do not set the `NPM_TOKEN` or `PYPI_TOKEN` secret. Remove it, or leave the repository secret undefined.
265	   - npm needs Node 22.14 or newer and npm 11.5.1 or newer for trusted publishing. Add a setup step to the `execute` job before the release step, for example:
266	
267	     ```yaml
268	     - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 # pin to a commit SHA
269	       with:
270	         node-version: '22.14'
271	     - run: npm install --global npm@^11.5.1
272	     ```
273	
274	   - PyPI needs a twine that supports trusted publishing. Generated workflows install `twine==7.0.0` in `execute`; a hand-written workflow must provide its own. Older twine releases were not checked.
275	3. **Limit.** With no token Callisto passes no `.npmrc` to the confirmation step, so a restricted scoped package may publish and then fail to confirm, because npm answers an anonymous view of it with 404. Not yet verified.
276	4. **Read auth stays separate.** Trusted publishing covers publishing only. A job that installs private dependencies still needs its own read credential (for example an `.npmrc` token with read access or a private index login) in the job that installs them, never in `execute`.
277	
278	---
279	
280	## Cargo (crates.io)
281	
282	Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:
283	
284	```yaml
285	env:
286	  CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
287	```
288	
289	Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. Inject it only into the job that publishes.
290	
291	---
292	
293	## Python (PyPI)
294	
295	Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):
296	
297	```yaml
298	env:
299	  TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
300	  TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
301	```
302	
303	Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognize that variable name.
304	
305	The release action maps the `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_USERNAME` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` itself. A workflow that runs `twine` directly must set both, because the secret name alone does not configure Twine.
306	
307	### Generated Callisto workflows
308	
309	Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing: `NPM_TOKEN` becomes an `.npmrc` entry that reads it, and `PYPI_TOKEN` becomes `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` with `TWINE_PASSWORD`. An unset or empty secret configures nothing, which leaves [tokenless trusted publishing](#tokenless-trusted-publishing) to the tools. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.
310	
311	`prepack` and `prepare` run in the job that packs the package, which has no registry credentials. `prepublishOnly`, `publish` and `postpublish` do not run, because the publish is `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`. A package that relied on a publish-time hook moves that work into `prepack`.
312	
313	### Current Python support limits
314	
315	Callisto supports static PEP 621 or Poetry versions with `python -m build` and Twine. Current limits:
316	
317	- Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects fail discovery with E007, including Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions.
318	- Without a sealed build, files an earlier attempt uploaded are matched by name, not by content: a rebuild is not always byte-identical. A package whose wheel name depends on the platform uploads another wheel when rerun on a different machine. A file this run uploads must match the digest the index serves for it; an index that serves no digest is accepted, because only sealed files require one. Builds set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time, which makes hatchling, poetry-core, uv_build and pdm-backend wheels, and setuptools wheels, repeat byte for byte; sdists from setuptools and pdm-backend still differ.
319	- Both generated workflows build in a job without credentials (`build-python` or `package`) and seal the files in the manifest. The executing job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. A manifest that is present but does not seal a Python publish of the plan fails the release (E306) before any build, so the build backend never runs beside the registry token. Without a manifest (the local `callisto release`), the files are built in a temporary directory with registry credentials withheld, then uploaded. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).
320	- npm is sealed the same way: `release pack-npm` packs each npm package and platform package, `artifact-manifest --seal-npm` records the tarballs, and `execute` publishes exactly those files after re-checking their sha256. A rerun in the same workflow run reuses the same tarballs; "Re-run all jobs" packs again, and a version the registry already shows is adopted by version, not by bytes.
321	- A release can only be completed for 14 days after its first file; after that, PyPI [refuses new files](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/) and the release needs a new version.
322	- A package tagged by an earlier version of callisto with only some of its files uploaded is reported as released when rerun at the same commit. Finish it by uploading the missing files with `twine`.
323	- A configured `url` is the simple index Callisto reads and, unless `publish-url` names another endpoint, the one Twine uploads to. Private indexes with read authentication or HTML-only responses need explicit support. Twine credentials do not authenticate `curl`.
324	- Dependencies in `[dependency-groups]`, Poetry groups and the legacy dev-dependency tables are not followed or rewritten when a workspace package is released. Under uv a version pin on a workspace member is ignored, and Poetry normally references siblings by path, so a stale pin there is harmless; a group that pins a registry version of a sibling is not updated.
325	- `release` refuses snapshot versions (E169), so a snapshot is never published. Python snapshots use a PEP 440 local label (`0.0.0.dev0+<tag>.<sha>`), which public PyPI would reject anyway. See [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).
326

# Releasing

How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.

For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).

---

## Local release: `callisto release`

`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.

- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
- `--package <ecosystem/name>` (repeatable) restricts the run to named unreleased packages, all distributions of each (naming `npm/dual` also releases `cargo/dual`), plus every member of their fixed or linked groups. An unreleased workspace package that a selected one depends on (runtime, optional, or peer) must be selected too.
- It refuses a dirty worktree: a tracked modification or an untracked file not covered by `.gitignore`. Ignored files never count.
- It requires the git repository root to be the workspace root; a workspace in a subdirectory fails with `E170`.
- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
- A workspace with artifact slots or napi platform packages must release through CI. See the generated workflow below.

`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.

A local release refuses with E320, before any effect, when the registry already holds a version it would release but the package's files changed since the commit that set that version, or no commit in this history sets it. Check out the version commit the error names and run `callisto release` again: it adopts the published version and tags that commit. When no commit is named, check out the commit that was published, or tag it by hand.

### Current retry limit

If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` at the same commit lists the package again, observes each remaining effect and finishes it.

- `Nothing to release.` is not proof of completion for a tag on an older commit: the retry looks only at tags on the commit being released.
- CI releases based on the merged release PR retain the original package list.

---

## Generated workflows

`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`; in a workspace that already has `callisto.toml` it writes only the workflow. Keep that filename for generated artifact releases.

Init never overwrites an existing file. This repo's [release workflow](../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) is a worked example.

- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `package` (no secrets) checks whether the commit adds or modifies the release decision, and if so plans the release, builds Python distributions and packs npm packages, and hands them to `execute`, which publishes exactly those files. On that push `version-pr` waits for `execute`, so the next release PR is built from the new tags. A push that merely contains an untagged version publishes nothing; recovery is "Re-run failed jobs".
- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan, build (read-only), attest (no checkout, no commands), optional Python build, crate packaging and npm pack jobs (no credentials), and execute. As in the simple shape, `version-pr` waits for `execute` on a release push. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.

Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).

Generated build support has these boundaries:

- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
- Custom artifact builders need `--no-workflow` and a manual workflow that fills every configured artifact slot.
- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.

The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.

Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. The action installs the release that commit belongs to. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.

Build-matrix limits:

- An addon crate outside the napi package directory needs a unique crate whose lib name matches `napi.binaryName` (E204).
- Generated `.node` files must be gitignored; release execution requires a clean checkout.
- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
- The napi build and placement roster comes from the release intent, so an unrelated addon does not block a release of another package.
- npm lifecycle hooks split at the pack. `prepack` and `prepare` run in the job that packs the package, which holds no registry credentials. The publish is `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`, so `prepublishOnly`, `publish` and `postpublish` no longer run. Move work that must happen before a release into `prepack`, and anything that acts on the registry into a step of your own after `execute`. Effects an owner-defined hook still has at pack time are outside Callisto's release graph.

---

## Release PR and approval

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

During a pre cycle (`callisto pre enter <tag>`) the release PR works the same way: a new changeset, or a new conventional commit to a `release-trigger = "auto"` package, opens or updates the release PR for the next prerelease, a cycle with nothing new since its last prerelease needs none, and after `callisto pre exit` the release PR releases the stable versions.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for a hand-written local workflow, and `execute` runs `callisto release execute` on the intent and files a credential-free job prepared. Generated workflows use plan/build/execute (build-matrix) or package/execute (simple). See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials or an OIDC token for publishing. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning, build, pack and attestation jobs, and action inputs. The attestation job holds `id-token: write`, so it has no checkout and runs no command.

After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

## PR pre-flight verification

[`.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml`](../.github/actions/callisto-validate/action.yml) is a reusable action for your PR workflow:

- `callisto status --check` — one gate covering config health, package discovery, and changeset syntax: exit 0 with no error-level diagnostics, exit 1 otherwise.
- `callisto status --check --since origin/main` — also fails when the pull request changes a package that no changeset names. A change that needs no release takes a changeset with severity `none`.
- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
- Writes a workspace status summary to the job's GitHub Actions summary page.

---

## Release identity and recovery

Every release run records two different revisions:

- The **orchestration revision**: the workflow and Callisto CLI that coordinate the run.
- The **release-source revision**: the merged release commit whose exact versions are released.

A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and the merged release PR's full source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code or invent a newer version. Callisto's own workflow asks [`callisto release pending`](#finding-releases-that-did-not-finish) for the oldest unfinished release on each main push. It verifies that SHA against the merged managed PR and the current main history before planning. After a release executes, the workflow dispatches the next unfinished one, or refreshes the release PR for newer changesets when none remains.

To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs" or dispatch the workflow on main with `release_source_sha=<merged PR merge SHA>`. Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds. The merge SHA is available in the PR's merge commit and does not depend on a proposed version tag. Release runs execute one at a time: a push during a release waits, then finds nothing pending. A dispatch with an explicit SHA queued behind a push can be replaced by it, so dispatch it again if it did not start.

A failed release is selected again on every main push until it finishes, which also holds back the release PR refresh. To get past one you finished by hand, push its missing tags, or run `callisto release pending --from <newer release sha>`. Otherwise recover it with a dispatch of its SHA (see [recovering an older release](#recovering-an-older-release)). Finish an older unpublished release before merging a newer release PR: the newer one publishes without any warning that the older version was never tagged.

Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.

## Finding releases that did not finish

`callisto release pending` lists the merged release commits whose release did not finish, oldest first, with what is missing. It reads each release commit's committed decision and checks that every package has its tag and every GitHub release is published, so it needs no checkout of the old commit and publishes nothing. A release publishes to the registries before it tags, so a missing tag means the release stopped early.

```sh
callisto release pending                    # text
callisto --format json release pending      # for a workflow
callisto release pending --from <sha>       # skip an older release that cannot finish
```

Recover each one with the dispatch below, oldest first.

## A stale release PR

Callisto's workflow rebuilds the release PR on every push to `main`. While that rebuild is pending the PR is stale: if changesets changed on `main` since it was built, merging it releases the wrong set. So a second workflow, `Hold release PR`, turns the open release PR into a draft the moment `main` moves, and the release workflow marks it ready only after a rebuild from the new tip. If the rebuild fails, the PR stays a draft and cannot be merged. Re-run that `Release` workflow run, and the PR becomes ready when it succeeds. A transient GitHub error during the rebuild is attempted up to four times in all before it fails.

If a stale release PR whose changesets were already consumed on `main` was merged anyway, the release fails with [E165](errors.md) because the changesets the merge deleted are not the ones its decision recorded, and every later push to `main` retries it. A stale PR that deletes no changesets, one that releases only bumps inferred from commits or a prerelease PR of a Changesets v2 pre cycle, gets no E165 from its changesets. E165 still refuses it when `main` already holds its versions, and `Hold release PR` keeps a stale PR in draft. Nothing was published. Revert the merge's release payload (the version bumps, changelog entries and `.callisto/release-decision.json`, not the changeset files) in a pull request to `main`. The next push rebuilds the release PR from the changesets that are really pending.

## Recovering an older release

Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:

**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:

```sh
SHA=<release-source sha>
git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
git push origin "<tag>"
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

**`ArtifactAssetDiffers`: rebuilt assets don't match.** Rebuilt tarballs aren't byte-identical. Delete the mismatched assets and dispatch again:

```sh
gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
gh workflow run callisto-release.yml --ref main -f release_source_sha="$SHA"
```

## Publication checks

Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.

Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.

---

## Platform-package publish order

`callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.

A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.

- **A platform package fails**: its owner's main package is never attempted, so no `optionalDependencies` point at a version that was never uploaded. Fix the cause and re-run — it adopts every effect that already landed.
- **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.

For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.
# Publishing: registry authentication

Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).

Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.

---

## First publish

A package that has never been published is released from its manifest version with no changeset. Callisto plans it like any other release, and the first publish is the one most likely to fail for reasons outside Callisto:

- **Check the name first.** A name another project already owns is rejected by the registry. If it already holds the version you are releasing under another repository, `callisto release` stops with E322 and names that repository. Search the registry before the first release.
- **Fill in the metadata the registry requires.** crates.io needs `description` and `license` (or `license-file`) in `Cargo.toml`. A first release of a crate without them stops with E323 before anything is published.
- **Use a token that can create the package.** A token scoped to existing packages cannot publish a new one. Trusted publishing (OIDC) is configured per package on the registry and generally needs the package, or a pending publisher, to exist first, so plan on one token-based first publish. Follow each registry's current documentation.
- **Package managers.** An npm package is packed with the manager its workspace uses (`npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` 4 or `bun`), so `workspace:` and `catalog:` ranges are rewritten in the tarball, and published by `npm` as `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`, passing `--tag`, `--access` and `--registry` when set. Authentication is `npm`'s: `NPM_TOKEN` through the project or user `.npmrc`, so a token kept only in `.yarnrc.yml` (`npmAuthToken`) or Bun's config is not used. `npm publish <tarball>` does not read a registry from `.yarnrc.yml` (`npmPublishRegistry`, `npmRegistryServer`, or either under `npmScopes`) or from `bunfig.toml`, so a yarn or bun workspace that sets one there is refused with E168 before anything is published. Set the registry as `publishConfig.registry` in the package's `package.json`, or in `.npmrc`.
- **Scoped npm packages** publish with `--access public` by default. A private scoped package sets `publishConfig.access` to `"restricted"` in its `package.json`, which Callisto passes through.
- **Rehearse.** `callisto release --dry-run` shows what would be published and in which order, and works without credentials.

## Pulling a release

Callisto never deletes, yanks or deprecates anything. Pulling a release is a manual registry action, and the version stays used:

| Registry | Soft pull | Delete |
| --- | --- | --- |
| crates.io | `cargo yank` hides it from new resolution; it stays downloadable and existing lockfiles keep working. | Limited to 72 hours after publishing, or a single owner, few downloads and no dependents. |
| npm | `npm deprecate` keeps it installable with a warning. | `npm unpublish` within 72 hours if nothing depends on it; later only with no dependents, under 300 weekly downloads and a single owner. A used version number can never be reused, and removing every version blocks the name for 24 hours. |
| PyPI | Yank (PEP 592) hides it from normal resolution. | Permanent. A filename cannot be reused even after deletion, and deleting a project frees its name for anyone. |

Registries cache their indexes for minutes, so a pulled version can keep appearing briefly. Prefer the soft pull, then release a fixed, higher version through the normal flow. Leave the git tag in place: Callisto treats an existing tag as a release already made. Yanking does not undo a leaked secret; rotate it.

If you remove a version that is still the manifest version, `callisto release` will try to finish it again and stop with an error. Bump the version with a changeset instead.

See the registries' own pages for current rules: [cargo yank](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-yank.html), [npm unpublish](https://docs.npmjs.com/policies/unpublish) and the [PyPI help](https://pypi.org/help/).

## Where a publish goes

A registry with no `url` in `callisto.toml` publishes wherever the checkout's own configuration says: `.npmrc` for npm. Callisto honors that on purpose, so a private registry set there keeps working, and it means that file decides where the registry token is sent. A Cargo package with `crates-io` in `publish-to` runs a plain `cargo publish`, so Cargo's own configuration (`publish` in `Cargo.toml`, `[registry] default`) can redirect it while Callisto still observes crates.io. To pin a destination, name a `[registries.<name>]` entry with `kind = "cargo"` in `publish-to`: Callisto then runs `cargo publish --registry <name>`, `.cargo/config.toml` decides that registry's URL and where its token is sent, and the release job needs `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN` (the name upper-cased, `-` as `_`). Review changes to them like code. A release pull request cannot carry such a change: a version commit may only touch manifests, lockfiles, changelogs, changesets and the decision file, and any other path fails verification with E165. For npm (except yarn) and PyPI, `url` on the registry entry names the registry Callisto reads and publishes to from `callisto.toml`. It does not override native routing: npm configuration such as `@scope:registry` in `.npmrc` still routes a scoped package, and Callisto respects that. Callisto adds no destination allowlist or preflight, so review changes to `.npmrc` like code. A named Cargo registry takes its URL only from `.cargo/config.toml`, and a `url` on a cargo registry is rejected.

---

## npm

Two supported patterns.

### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`

Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:

```yaml
- name: Authenticate with npm registry
  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
  env:
    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
```

`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.

### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`

`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:

```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  with:
    node-version: '20'
    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.

### Choosing a pattern

| Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
| Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
| Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
| Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |

### Provenance

Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.

### Tokenless trusted publishing

npm and PyPI can publish without a stored token: the registry trusts the workflow's OIDC identity. The native tools own that authentication. Callisto adds no auth switch or broker; it keeps the `execute` job's OIDC request variables for `npm` and `twine`, and when `NPM_TOKEN` or `PYPI_TOKEN` is empty or unset it configures no token, so the tool falls back to OIDC.

Hosted OIDC publishing is not yet verified against the real registries. Rehearse it on a throwaway package before relying on it.

1. **Registry side.** Add a trusted publisher for the package on the registry.
   - npm: bind it to the release workflow file (`callisto-release.yml`), and to the GitHub environment too if the `execute` job uses one.
   - PyPI: add a trusted publisher naming the repository, the workflow file and, if used, the environment. A package that does not exist yet needs a pending publisher.
2. **Workflow side.**
   - `execute` needs `permissions: id-token: write`; generated workflows grant it.
   - Do not set the `NPM_TOKEN` or `PYPI_TOKEN` secret. Remove it, or leave the repository secret undefined.
   - npm needs Node 22.14 or newer and npm 11.5.1 or newer for trusted publishing. Add a setup step to the `execute` job before the release step, for example:

     ```yaml
     - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 # pin to a commit SHA
       with:
         node-version: '22.14'
     - run: npm install --global npm@^11.5.1
     ```

   - PyPI needs a twine that supports trusted publishing. Generated workflows install `twine==7.0.0` in `execute`; a hand-written workflow must provide its own. Older twine releases were not checked.
3. **Limit.** With no token Callisto passes no `.npmrc` to the confirmation step, so a restricted scoped package may publish and then fail to confirm, because npm answers an anonymous view of it with 404. Not yet verified.
4. **Read auth stays separate.** Trusted publishing covers publishing only. A job that installs private dependencies still needs its own read credential (for example an `.npmrc` token with read access or a private index login) in the job that installs them, never in `execute`.

---

## Cargo (crates.io)

Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:

```yaml
env:
  CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
```

Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. Inject it only into the job that publishes.

---

## Python (PyPI)

Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):

```yaml
env:
  TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
  TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
```

Do not use `TWINE_API_TOKEN` — twine does not recognize that variable name.

The release action maps the `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_USERNAME` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` itself. A workflow that runs `twine` directly must set both, because the secret name alone does not configure Twine.

### Generated Callisto workflows

Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing: `NPM_TOKEN` becomes an `.npmrc` entry that reads it, and `PYPI_TOKEN` becomes `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` with `TWINE_PASSWORD`. An unset or empty secret configures nothing, which leaves [tokenless trusted publishing](#tokenless-trusted-publishing) to the tools. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.

`prepack` and `prepare` run in the job that packs the package, which has no registry credentials. `prepublishOnly`, `publish` and `postpublish` do not run, because the publish is `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`. A package that relied on a publish-time hook moves that work into `prepack`.

### Current Python support limits

Callisto supports static PEP 621 or Poetry versions with `python -m build` and Twine. Current limits:

- Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects fail discovery with E007, including Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions.
- Without a sealed build, files an earlier attempt uploaded are matched by name, not by content: a rebuild is not always byte-identical. A package whose wheel name depends on the platform uploads another wheel when rerun on a different machine. A file this run uploads must match the digest the index serves for it; an index that serves no digest is accepted, because only sealed files require one. Builds set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time, which makes hatchling, poetry-core, uv_build and pdm-backend wheels, and setuptools wheels, repeat byte for byte; sdists from setuptools and pdm-backend still differ.
- Both generated workflows build in a job without credentials (`build-python` or `package`) and seal the files in the manifest. The executing job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. A manifest that is present but does not seal a Python publish of the plan fails the release (E306) before any build, so the build backend never runs beside the registry token. Without a manifest (the local `callisto release`), the files are built in a temporary directory with registry credentials withheld, then uploaded. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).
- npm is sealed the same way: `release pack-npm` packs each npm package and platform package, `artifact-manifest --seal-npm` records the tarballs, and `execute` publishes exactly those files after re-checking their sha256. A rerun in the same workflow run reuses the same tarballs; "Re-run all jobs" packs again, and a version the registry already shows is adopted by version, not by bytes.
- A release can only be completed for 14 days after its first file; after that, PyPI [refuses new files](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/) and the release needs a new version.
- A package tagged by an earlier version of callisto with only some of its files uploaded is reported as released when rerun at the same commit. Finish it by uploading the missing files with `twine`.
- A configured `url` is the simple index Callisto reads and, unless `publish-url` names another endpoint, the one Twine uploads to. Private indexes with read authentication or HTML-only responses need explicit support. Twine credentials do not authenticate `curl`.
- Dependencies in `[dependency-groups]`, Poetry groups and the legacy dev-dependency tables are not followed or rewritten when a workspace package is released. Under uv a version pin on a workspace member is ignored, and Poetry normally references siblings by path, so a stale pin there is harmless; a group that pins a registry version of a sibling is not updated.
- `release` refuses snapshot versions (E169), so a snapshot is never published. Python snapshots use a PEP 440 local label (`0.0.0.dev0+<tag>.<sha>`), which public PyPI would reject anyway. See [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).

# Configuration reference

Every key `callisto.toml` accepts, from `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/{raw,resolve,groups}.rs`. Unknown keys are rejected (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`).

This reference describes current keys, not the unimplemented parts of the [polyglot design](architecture/polyglot-v1.md). Every package named in this file must be written `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name`; a bare name is E317 and the colon form is E316. No release-owner, generic build-input or per-file PyPI configuration exists.

## Top-level tables

| Table | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[changesets]` | table | no | Where changesets live |
| `[cascade]` | table | no | Dependency-bump cascade policy |
| `[validation]` | table | no | Status/version validation policy |
| `[changelog]` | table | no | Layout of the changelog sections `callisto version` writes |
| `[release]` | table | no | Product binary release declaration |
| `[registries]` | table of tables | no | Registry endpoint overrides |
| `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package overrides, matched by exact name or by glob |
| `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
| `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |

## `[changesets]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |

Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.

## `[cascade]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
| `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
| `peer-escalation` | bool | `false` | Escalate an out-of-range peer-dependency bump to a major bump for the dependent; off, the dependent gets `bump-severity` |
| `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |

Example:
```toml
[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true
```

## `[validation]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |

## `[changelog]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | string (`"grouped"` \| `"flat"`) | `"grouped"` | `grouped` writes a date line (with a compare link when the repository is known, from `[release] forge-repository` or else the GitHub `origin` remote, and the previous version has a tag), then `### Major Changes`, `### Minor Changes` and `### Patch Changes` groups, omitting empty ones; dependency updates sit under Patch Changes; a package that only released with its group has no groups, just that line. `flat` writes one bullet list under the version heading, as before layouts existed. Sections already in a changelog are never rewritten. |

Example: `layout = "flat"`.

## `[release]`

Credentials and registry endpoints are deliberately excluded — this table only declares immutable intent slots; execution receives credentials from its caller.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
| `forge-repository` | string | origin's GitHub repository | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to; a release always publishes to origin's GitHub repository, so the key changes only the compare-link repository when it differs from origin's |
| `targets` | array of strings | `[]` | Target triples the product is built for. Needs `asset-name` |
| `asset-name` | string | none | Names each of `targets`; `{target}` is the only placeholder. Needs `targets` |
| `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Another package's artifact, or an irregular name such as a Windows `.zip` (see below) |

At least one target or artifact is required. A target in `targets` that a `[[release.artifact]]` also names for the same package is an error (E197).

### `[[release.artifact]]`

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
| `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
| `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
targets = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"]
asset-name = "callisto-{target}.tar.gz"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
target = "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"
asset-name = "callisto-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip"
```

## `[registries]`

Keyed by registry name: letters, digits, `-` and `_`, not starting with `-`. Three registries are predeclared: `crates-io` (kind `cargo`), `npm` (kind `npm`) and `pypi` (kind `pypi`). They exist even without a `[registries]` table; a `[registries.<predeclared>]` entry configures that registry and may leave `kind` out. Any other name fails with E325 when it is not a valid name, is a `publish-to` word (`github-release`, `none`), or is the old `cratesIo` spelling.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | required, except for `crates-io`, `npm` and `pypi`, which default to their own kind | Registry ecosystem. A custom registry without it fails with E321. A predeclared registry given another kind fails with E334 |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `npm` it is the registry the publish and the confirmation use. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set. A `cargo` registry rejects it with E336: cargo takes its URL from `.cargo/config.toml`, and a package publishes to the registry by naming it in `publish-to` |
| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |
| `registries.<name>.publish-timeout` | string | `15m` | The longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run before Callisto stops it with E025. Same format and range as `confirm-timeout` |
| `registries.<name>.confirm-timeout` | string | `6m` for `npm` and `pypi`, `2m` for `cargo` | How long Callisto waits for a version it just published to appear on the registry before failing with E157. A whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from `1s` to `1h`. npm serves package documents from a cache that can answer stale for up to 5 minutes; raise it for a slower registry, and keep the release job's `timeout-minutes` above it |

For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

A named `kind = "npm"` or `kind = "pypi"` registry cannot be a `publish-to` target (E330). A named npm registry's `url` only approves a package's `publishConfig.registry`; a named pypi registry does nothing yet.

Example:
```toml
[registries.internal-npm]
kind = "npm"
url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
```

A private Cargo registry is named in `publish-to`, and its URL is defined in `.cargo/config.toml` under `[registries.internal-crates]`:
```toml
[registries.internal-crates]
kind = "cargo"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/my-crate"
publish-to = ["internal-crates"]
```

## `[[package]]`

A `match` is either exact or a glob; a `match` containing any of `*?[]{}` is a glob. An exact `match` is an ecosystem-qualified id: the package's own name in that ecosystem, which for a dual package can differ per ecosystem. A glob `match` is an ecosystem-qualified glob, compared with each package's name in that ecosystem, and can match many packages at once; a rule for several ecosystems is one rule per ecosystem.

An exact rule wins over any glob, whatever the declaration order. Otherwise the first matching rule in declaration order wins. The winning rule applies whole: fields are not merged across rules.

`[[package-set]]` is no longer a key: it is E325. Rename each `[[package-set]]` to `[[package]]`; its `match` already holds a glob.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string | required | `ecosystem/name`, or `ecosystem/glob`. The ecosystem is `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; a name without one is E317. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"github-release"` \| `"none"`, or a registry name: `"crates-io"`, `"npm"`, `"pypi"` or a `kind = "cargo"` `[registries]` entry) | none | Where this package publishes. Any other value fails with E330 |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | Exact `match` only; a glob is E338. Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`

Neither has a config-level default for its fields — both are required when the block is present.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
| `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | `ecosystem/name` of each package in the group. A platform package is named by its native name |

`[[fixed-group]]`: all members bump in lock-step from the group's alignment base. `[[linked-group]]`: every member receives the highest severity and aligns to the highest target version produced by the members' bumps. Both currently require compatible version grammars; neither is an automatic cross-language version converter.

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[fixed-group]]
name = "workspace"
members = ["cargo/callisto-model", "cargo/callisto-manifests", "cargo/callisto-graph", "cargo/callisto-cli", "cargo/callisto-fixtures"]
```

## Migrating from Changesets

`callisto init` reads `.changeset/config.json` from `@changesets/cli` 2.x and 3.x. The `.changeset/*.md` files need no conversion.

| Changesets key | `init` does |
| --- | --- |
| `fixed` | Writes `[[fixed-group]]` entries named `fixed-<n>`. Names are npm package names. Globs expand to the npm packages that exist now, so add packages created later by hand. A group using `!`, `{`, `[` or `(` (negation, braces, classes, extglobs) is not written: the warning gives the block to paste once you have checked its members. |
| `linked` | Warns and writes nothing. A callisto linked group bumps every member on each release, and Changesets bumps only members with changesets. |
| `ignore` | Warns and writes nothing. An ignored package is still versioned; `publish-to = ["none"]` stops its publishing. |

## Identity and defaults

Unspecified package fields are filled during graph construction: the release trigger defaults to changesets, the changelog to the package directory, and publish targets to those declared by its manifests. Default tags use the display id, so newly created tags become qualified after name promotion; historical bare tags use the ownership fallback described in [identity](architecture/identity.md). # Configuration reference

Every key `callisto.toml` accepts, from `crates/callisto-graph/src/config/{raw,resolve,groups}.rs`. Unknown keys are rejected (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`).

This reference describes current keys, not the unimplemented parts of the [polyglot design](architecture/polyglot-v1.md). Every package named in this file must be written `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name`; a bare name is E317 and the colon form is E316. No release-owner, generic build-input or per-file PyPI configuration exists.

## Top-level tables

| Table | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[changesets]` | table | no | Where changesets live |
| `[cascade]` | table | no | Dependency-bump cascade policy |
| `[validation]` | table | no | Status/version validation policy |
| `[changelog]` | table | no | Layout of the changelog sections `callisto version` writes |
| `[release]` | table | no | Product binary release declaration |
| `[registries]` | table of tables | no | Registry endpoint overrides |
| `[[package]]` | array of tables | no | Per-package overrides, matched by exact name or by glob |
| `[[fixed-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that version in lock-step |
| `[[linked-group]]` | array of tables | no | Packages that share severity, not version |

## `[changesets]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string | `.changeset` | Workspace-root-relative changeset directory. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E116). |

Example: `dir = ".changeset"`.

## `[cascade]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string (`"out-of-range"` \| `"always"`) | `"out-of-range"` | When a dependency bump forces a cascading bump on dependents |
| `bump-severity` | string (`"patch"` \| `"minor"`) | `"patch"` | Severity applied to a cascaded bump |
| `peer-escalation` | bool | `false` | Escalate an out-of-range peer-dependency bump to a major bump for the dependent; off, the dependent gets `bump-severity` |
| `preserve-npm-ranges` | bool | `true` | Keep existing npm semver range operators (`^`, `~`) when rewriting dependency versions |

Example:
```toml
[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true
```

## `[validation]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allow-empty-changesets` | bool | `false` | Allow `callisto version` to run with zero pending changesets (also settable per-invocation via `--allow-empty-changesets`) |

## `[changelog]`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | string (`"grouped"` \| `"flat"`) | `"grouped"` | `grouped` writes a date line (with a compare link when the repository is known, from `[release] forge-repository` or else the GitHub `origin` remote, and the previous version has a tag), then `### Major Changes`, `### Minor Changes` and `### Patch Changes` groups, omitting empty ones; dependency updates sit under Patch Changes; a package that only released with its group has no groups, just that line. `flat` writes one bullet list under the version heading, as before layouts existed. Sections already in a changelog are never rewritten. |

Example: `layout = "flat"`.

## `[release]`

Credentials and registry endpoints are deliberately excluded — this table only declares immutable intent slots; execution receives credentials from its caller.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `product-package` | string | required | Ecosystem-qualified package whose binaries ship as release assets, e.g. `cargo/callisto-cli` |
| `forge-repository` | string | origin's GitHub repository | `owner/repo` the product release publishes to; a release always publishes to origin's GitHub repository, so the key changes only the compare-link repository when it differs from origin's |
| `targets` | array of strings | `[]` | Target triples the product is built for. Needs `asset-name` |
| `asset-name` | string | none | Names each of `targets`; `{target}` is the only placeholder. Needs `targets` |
| `[[release.artifact]]` | array of tables | `[]` | Another package's artifact, or an irregular name such as a Windows `.zip` (see below) |

At least one target or artifact is required. A target in `targets` that a `[[release.artifact]]` also names for the same package is an error (E197).

### `[[release.artifact]]`

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `package` | string | yes | Ecosystem-qualified package that builds this artifact (need not be `product-package`) |
| `target` | string | yes | Opaque target triple — passed through to the builder, never parsed by Callisto |
| `asset-name` | string | yes | Exact GitHub release asset filename |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[release]
product-package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
targets = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"]
asset-name = "callisto-{target}.tar.gz"

[[release.artifact]]
package = "cargo/callisto-cli"
target = "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"
asset-name = "callisto-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip"
```

## `[registries]`

Keyed by registry name: letters, digits, `-` and `_`, not starting with `-`. Three registries are predeclared: `crates-io` (kind `cargo`), `npm` (kind `npm`) and `pypi` (kind `pypi`). They exist even without a `[registries]` table; a `[registries.<predeclared>]` entry configures that registry and may leave `kind` out. Any other name fails with E325 when it is not a valid name, is a `publish-to` word (`github-release`, `none`), or is the old `cratesIo` spelling.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | required, except for `crates-io`, `npm` and `pypi`, which default to their own kind | Registry ecosystem. A custom registry without it fails with E321. A predeclared registry given another kind fails with E334 |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override. For `npm` it is the registry the publish and the confirmation use. For `pypi` it is the simple index Callisto reads, and the upload endpoint unless `publish-url` is set. A `cargo` registry rejects it with E336: cargo takes its URL from `.cargo/config.toml`, and a package publishes to the registry by naming it in `publish-to` |
| `registries.<name>.publish-url` | string | `url` | `pypi` only: the endpoint Twine uploads to when it differs from the index. Same HTTPS rules as `url` |
| `registries.<name>.publish-timeout` | string | `15m` | The longest one publish command (`cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `twine upload`) may run before Callisto stops it with E025. Same format and range as `confirm-timeout` |
| `registries.<name>.confirm-timeout` | string | `6m` for `npm` and `pypi`, `2m` for `cargo` | How long Callisto waits for a version it just published to appear on the registry before failing with E157. A whole number with `s`, `m` or `h`, from `1s` to `1h`. npm serves package documents from a cache that can answer stale for up to 5 minutes; raise it for a slower registry, and keep the release job's `timeout-minutes` above it |

For `pypi`, set `publish-url` when the index and the upload endpoint differ, for example `url = "https://test.pypi.org/simple"` with `publish-url = "https://test.pypi.org/legacy/"`; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).

A named `kind = "npm"` or `kind = "pypi"` registry cannot be a `publish-to` target (E330). A named npm registry's `url` only approves a package's `publishConfig.registry`; a named pypi registry does nothing yet.

Example:
```toml
[registries.internal-npm]
kind = "npm"
url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
```

A private Cargo registry is named in `publish-to`, and its URL is defined in `.cargo/config.toml` under `[registries.internal-crates]`:
```toml
[registries.internal-crates]
kind = "cargo"

[[package]]
match = "cargo/my-crate"
publish-to = ["internal-crates"]
```

## `[[package]]`

A `match` is either exact or a glob; a `match` containing any of `*?[]{}` is a glob. An exact `match` is an ecosystem-qualified id: the package's own name in that ecosystem, which for a dual package can differ per ecosystem. A glob `match` is an ecosystem-qualified glob, compared with each package's name in that ecosystem, and can match many packages at once; a rule for several ecosystems is one rule per ecosystem.

An exact rule wins over any glob, whatever the declaration order. Otherwise the first matching rule in declaration order wins. The winning rule applies whole: fields are not merged across rules.

`[[package-set]]` is no longer a key: it is E325. Rename each `[[package-set]]` to `[[package]]`; its `match` already holds a glob.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string | required | `ecosystem/name`, or `ecosystem/glob`. The ecosystem is `cargo`, `npm` or `pypi`; a name without one is E317. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"github-release"` \| `"none"`, or a registry name: `"crates-io"`, `"npm"`, `"pypi"` or a `kind = "cargo"` `[registries]` entry) | none | Where this package publishes. Any other value fails with E330 |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | Exact `match` only; a glob is E338. Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |

```toml
[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

| `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | `ecosystem/name` of each package in the group. A platform package is named by its native name |
